title: Voices from the river town
paragraphs: While reorganising a storeroom, the community library in a river town found a cardboard box of cassette tapes recorded almost forty years earlier. A teacher named Suriati had interviewed boat builders, market traders and residents who remembered major floods. Several tape cases were cracked and their paper labels had faded. The librarian described the collection as fragile because further heat and moisture could easily damage it.

A group of secondary-school students offered to help identify the recordings. Some labels were cryptic: one read only “north landing, first flood”, without a date or speaker's name. Instead of guessing, the students listed every clue and compared names with old yearbooks and local newspaper reports. This cautious approach allowed them to separate evidence from assumptions.

Digitising each tape required a meticulous process. The students cleaned the playback equipment, assigned a number to every cassette, copied it once at a stable speed and logged the exact start and end times. Their careful routine reduced unnecessary handling and ensured that another researcher could follow what they had done.

Even after digitisation, some voices remained faint beneath bursts of static. The students therefore treated their first transcripts as tentative rather than final, placing uncertain words in brackets. They later invited older residents to listen. When several residents independently recognised the same speaker, their accounts corroborated the students' identification by providing additional support for it.

By the end of the project, visitors could search short summaries and listen to selected recordings through library headphones. The digital copies made the collection more accessible, while the original tapes stayed in controlled storage. The project did not recover every missing detail, but it preserved records that might otherwise have been lost. By documenting uncertainty openly, the students made the archive more trustworthy rather than less valuable.
